moat_against: Per-project bidding vs Array, GameChange, Arctech — no lock-in beyond backlog
Gross margin flattered by IRA 45X credits / tariff recoveries (~$99M in Q1 FY27) that management expects to normalize
83% U.S. revenue concentration — full exposure to U.S. tax-credit, tariff and permitting policy
SBC rising fast ($32M FY23 to $128M TTM) and share count +1.54%/yr dilute OE/share compounding
High-ROIC record is only three clean years — pre-IPO Flex capital structure makes earlier ROIC meaningless
moat_for: Global tracker leader (~26% share) — scale, bankability and field record developers pay for
TrueCapture / Hail Pro software and integrated bundles (tracker + eBOS + foundations) raise switching friction
Proven pricing power — gross margin 15.1% (FY23) to 32.6% (FY26) / 33.4% TTM
ROIC proxy 72.0% / 59.2% / 46.2% (FY24-26), far above cost of capital, on an asset-light model
Net-cash, investment-grade balance sheet and >$5.5B backlog
moat_justification: Clear #1 global tracker share (~26%), bankability and TrueCapture software with ROIC proxy 46-72% in the clean post-IPO years (FY24-26) and gross margin expanded to ~33%, but trackers are bid project-by-project, margins are partly policy-made (45X credits), and there is no recurring-revenue lock-in.
